name: Regular I Wedge Right
purpose: Short yardage and the goal line. Nobody blocks a man — the whole line squeezes shoulder to shoulder on the center and pushes. The tailback puts a hand on the center's back and goes wherever the pile goes.

C.note: You are the tip of the wedge — everybody else comes to you. Fire off the snap with your pads under whoever is on you.

Z.note: Tuck in tight behind the end. Nobody comes around the outside into the back of the wedge.

QB.rule: Snap, hand it to the tailback right now, and stay out of his way. Do not ride the handoff — he is already moving.

FB.note: Get in behind the wedge with both hands on the tailback's back and drive your legs. You are pushing him, not blocking anybody.

TB.rule: Put a hand on the center's back, get your pads low, and follow the wedge. Do not cut, do not bounce, do not look for a hole — the hole moves with you.

coaching_points: Two yards is a good wedge. Do not call it needing four.
Expect the heaviest front the league allows inside the five. It does not change the call — nobody is picking a man anyway.
Nothing in the league rulebook prohibits wedge blocking for 11-man play, but it is the first thing leagues take away. Re-check it every season before you install it.
Coach the shoulders, not the feet. If there is daylight between two linemen the wedge is a line of five men getting pushed backwards instead of one thing moving forward.
Low pads win this and nothing else does. The team that stands up loses.
